skills.name: Motives for the European scramble for Africa

note.text: European expansion had interacting economic, political and social or ideological motives. Firms sought markets, raw materials and profitable opportunities. Governments pursued prestige, strategic positions and advantage against rivals. Missionary ambitions and claims of a civilising mission supplied ideological arguments; racist assumptions were used to justify unequal rule. No single motive explains every region or actor. Distinguish the reasons actors gave publicly from the interests and actions supported by evidence.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: European expansion had interacting economic, political and social or ideological motives. Firms sought markets, raw materials and profitable opportunities. Governments pursued prestige, strategic positions and advantage against rivals. Missionary ambitions and claims of a civilising mission supplied ideological arguments; racist assumptions were used to justify unequal rule. No single motive explains every region or actor. Distinguish the reasons actors gave publicly from the interests and actions supported by evidence.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A merchant's request for protected trade, a government's concern over a rival flag and a mission appeal for conversion point to different motives. They could reinforce one another. Explaining an imperial ideology does not mean accepting its racist premises or treating colonisation as a benevolent necessity.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Classify the evidence rather than guessing from nationality. Ask whether it concerns commercial gain, power and security, or beliefs and claimed duties. Consider a combination when a case supports several motives. Avoid the claim that every European or every African shared one identical purpose.
